title: Question 4

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the features of the line in Fig. 4.2 that demonstrate that the motion of the trolley is simple harmonic.
hints: Hint 1: Start by recalling in words what has to be true about acceleration and displacement for any SHM motion, especially the direction of acceleration relative to displacement.
Hint 2: Look at the shape of the line in Fig. 4.2 - what does a straight line through the origin tell you about proportionality, and what does falling from left to right tell you about sign?
parts.proper_answer: The graph is a straight line through the origin with negative gradient, showing $a$ is proportional to $-x$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall what makes motion simple harmonic**
For SHM the acceleration must always point back toward the equilibrium position. That means when $x$ is positive, $a$ is negative, and when $x$ is negative, $a$ is positive. The size of $a$ must also grow in direct proportion to the size of $x$.

Step 2: **Read those two features from Fig. 4.2**
The line passes straight through the origin $(0,0)$, so $$a \propto x$$ in magnitude. It slopes downwards from left to right, so $a$ has the opposite sign to $x$. Together this is $$a = -\text{constant} \times x$$ which is the defining test for SHM.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use Fig. 4.2 to determine the period $T$ of the oscillations of the trolley.
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the link between the gradient of an $a$ against $x$ graph and the angular frequency in SHM.
Hint 2: Pick one clear point from Fig. 4.2, for example the end where $x = 12\text{ cm}$ and $a = 0.80\text{ m s}^{-2}$ in magnitude, and remember to convert $x$ to metres before comparing.
Hint 3: Once you have $\omega$, use the standard relation between $\omega$ and period $T$ to finish.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Connect the graph gradient to omega**
In SHM: $$a = -\omega^2 x$$ So the magnitude of the gradient of the $a$ against $x$ graph equals $\omega^2$. You just need $|a|/|x|$ for any point on the line.

Step 2: **Read values and convert units**
At the extreme, $|x| = 12\text{ cm} = 0.12\text{ m}$ gives $|a| = 0.80\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Therefore: $$\omega^2 = \frac{|a|}{|x|} = \frac{0.80}{0.12}$$ $$\omega = \sqrt{6.67} \approx 2.58\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$

Step 3: **Convert angular frequency to period**
Use: $$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}$$ $$T = \frac{2\pi}{2.58} \approx 2.4\text{ s}$$ This is the time for one complete back-and-forth oscillation.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: On the line of the graph of Fig. 4.2, label with the letter P one point where the kinetic energy of the trolley is zero.

markscheme_points.text: Point labelled P at one end of the lir

hints: Hint 1: Think about where in the swing the trolley momentarily stops to turn around, so its speed and kinetic energy are zero.
parts.proper_answer: P at either end of the line, at $x = +12\text{ cm}$ or $x = -12\text{ cm}$, where $a$ is maximum.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Locate zero speed**
Kinetic energy is zero when speed $v = 0$. That happens only at the turning points, the amplitude positions where the trolley is farthest from equilibrium. On Fig. 4.2 these are the two ends of the line at $x = \pm 12\text{ cm}$. Label either end P.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On the line of the graph of Fig. 4.2, label with the letter Q an approximate position of one point where the kinetic energy of the trolley is equal to the potential energy stored in the springs.

markscheme_points.text: Point labelled Q at displacement wit

hints: Hint 1: Think about how total energy is shared - all potential at the ends and all kinetic at the centre - so equal sharing must happen about halfway in energy terms, between centre and end.
parts.proper_answer: Q at $x \approx \pm 8.5\text{ cm}$ on the line, about $8$ to $9\text{ cm}$ from the origin.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find the equal-energy position**
At the centre all energy is kinetic, at the ends all energy is potential. Equal $KE$ and $PE$ occurs in between, where $$x = \frac{x_0}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \times 12\text{ cm} \approx 8.5\text{ cm}$$ So label Q on the line at about $x = +8.5\text{ cm}$ or $x = -8.5\text{ cm}$.

key_concepts: KE equals PE at x = amplitude / sqrt(2)
